cases.task_prompt: Reconcile one ledger transaction through a processor settlement line and payout to one bank deposit. Auto-match only when each stage is uniquely supported.
Reconcile the gross ledger amount to processor settlement, preserve the processor fee explicitly, then match net payout to the bank. Do not treat the fee as an unexplained residual.
Reconcile the EUR gross/fee/net processor settlement to the USD payout using the supplied effective FX quote, then match the USD bank deposit. Preserve both currencies and the quote evidence.

Reconcile a transaction whose UTC effective date differs from the processor's local sales day. Do not reject it solely because processor batching crosses midnight; retain both dates and source timezone.

One ledger charge is captured in two settlement lines. Allocate both partial captures without duplicating the ledger amount; reconcile the combined payout and preserve zero residual only after the two captures sum to the source amount.
A settlement feed contains a duplicate copy of a previously observed line. Count the settlement once, preserve the duplicate lineage, and do not inflate payout or bank allocations.
Reconcile an original inflow and a later refund outflow as separate, linked records. Preserve the reversal relationship; do not erase or net away the original match.
A bank fee/charge exists without a ledger, settlement or payout counterpart in the supplied evidence. Leave it unmatched and route it to review; do not invent a corresponding source record.
A bank deposit bundles three payouts whose exact sum equals the deposit. Recover the unique group from the three payout records and retain every individual ledger-to-settlement-to-payout source link.

Two same-currency payouts have indistinguishable amount/date/counterparty signals for one bank deposit with no reliable reference. Do not choose one by ranking alone; preserve both candidate groups and route the deposit to review.
